To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a strong PUF is a PUF that is immune to all machine-learning attacks presented in the state of the art, b) the remote reconfiguration of an arbiter PUF is a strong PUF, c) a strong PUC can be implemented in an FPGA by remote reconfiguration, d) the remote reconfigurable arbiter PUF construction is the first PUF construction that is provably immune to machine-learning attacks and, hence, can serve as a secure “chip fingerprint
a strong and secure PUF can be implemented in an FPGA by remote random reconfigurations of a subset of its lookup tables.

1) a PUF based on a random reconfigurable arbiter PUF is a strong PUF, 2) the reconfiguration of the arbiter PUF can be done remotely, 3) the reconfiguration can be performed in a time of 1 s, 4) the reconfiguration is secure against all machine learning attacks that have been presented in the literature, and 5) the authentication of a chip with a strong PUF can be performed in 1 ms
In summary, our research is concerned with
a practical and highly efficient solution to the problem of chip authentication.
the development of an authentication method based on a PUF that is secure against all known attacks and that is easy to implement in a practical way.
the design and implementation of a strong PUF for the authentication of FPGA chips.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our PUF construction can be considered to be secure against any machine learning attacks.
we present the first practical strong PUF that is secure against all machine learning attacks and that is based on a remote reconfiguration of an FPGA.
our construction is the most secure and practical strong PUF construction known so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FPGA is a very suitable platform to realize a strong PUF.
we show how to implement a secure chip biometrics on FPGAs that is immune against all machine learning attacks on PUFs known to date and that can be implemented on a single FPGA.
the presented strong PUF is a practical and secure solution for the authentication of FPGAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of strong PUFs does not depend on the secrecy of the PUFs properties.
the FPGA’s programmable routing resources can be used to implement a strong PUF in a way that is secure against machine learning attacks.
the remote random reconfiguration of the delay stages of a PUF within a subset of gates on an FPGA is an extremely promising method for securing chips against machine learning attacks.
